newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-VOELLER SAYS SECOND PLACE BETTER FOR BAYERN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-VOELLER SAYS SECOND PLACE BETTER FOR BAYERN.

text.p: Bayer Leverkusen's sporting director Rudi Voeller said it would be better for rivals Bayern Munich if they did not win the German soccer league.

"In Bayern, nerves are frazzled because there are several things in that team which don't go together," said the former World Cup striker in an interview with the German weekly Sport Bild on Wednesday.

"It would be better for Bayern to finish second because it would allow them to start all over again from scratch", he said, referring to recent conflicts within the Munich club. "That would do them good."
Bayern are currently top but Leverkusen are only one point behind with two games remaining. Bayern host VfB Stuttgart at the weekend while Leverkusen travel to neighbours Cologne.
Bayern have a tougher last two games than Leverkusen and their title challenge is undermined by a poor atmosphere in the club.

Club president Franz Beckenbauer recently criticised his players and striker Juergen Klinsmann said his frustration at Bayern's defensive tactics was one of the reasons for his decision to join Italian club Sampdoria next season.
"I don't feel that what Franz (Beckenbauer) did was that serious," said Voeller.

"As the president, he had the right (to do so). I've experienced things much worse than that. With Marseille, we lost 1-0 at home to Nantes once. Our president, Bernard Tapie, was so mad that he locked us up in our dressing room for two hours."
Voeller, 37, left Marseille in 1994 for Leverkusen and played for them for two seasons before starting a new career as their sporting director.
Leverkusen, who just avoided relegation last season, have never won the championship although they have triumphed on the European stage, winning the UEFA Cup in 1988.
Voeller said one of Bayern's main problems was that coach Giovanni Trapattoni and Klinsmann did not get on well.

"Everybody knows that when they were together at Internazionale, they already weren't on the same wave length," he said. "That hasn't changed. Klinsmann has had problems with Trapattoni for the whole season."
Klinsmann's problems did not stop him from scoring a superb goal to help Bayern to a convincing 3-0 victory at Hansa Rostock last Friday.
